verifications.claim: The Artemis II launch is from Kennedy Space Center.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'launch from Kennedy Space Center in Florida'; R3: 'Kennedy Space Center in Cape Canaveral, Florida'; R4: 'from Florida's Kennedy Space Center'; R5: 'Kennedy Space Center in Florida'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state the launch location as Kennedy Space Center.

verifications.claim: The target for the Artemis II launch is April 1, 2026, 6:24 p.m. ET.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: '6:24 p.m. ET today, Wednesday, April 1, 2026'; R3: '6:24 p.m. Eastern time ... April 1 at 6:24 pm'; R4: 'Wednesday, April 1, at 6:24 p.m.'; R5: '6:24 p.m. EDT Wednesday'
verifications.reasoning: Exact date, time, and ET specified across multiple sources.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II rocket travels east.
verifications.label: CLEAR

verifications.claim: The Artemis II launch has potential visibility for up to 70 seconds after liftoff.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Launch + 70 seconds'; R4: 'first 70 seconds'; R5: '10 seconds to 70 seconds after liftoff'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state maximum visibility up to 70 seconds.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II launch is best viewed 10-20 seconds after liftoff from the Space Coast, Orlando, Kissimmee, and Daytona Beach areas.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: '1: Launch + 10 seconds, Space Coast, east Orlando; 2: Launch + 20 seconds, Space Coast, Orlando, ... Kissimmee, ... Daytona Beach'; 'best see this moment in person, particularly ... Space Coast ... Daytona Beach area'
verifications.reasoning: Direct mapping of 10-20s visibility to exact areas listed; 'best' implied by proximity.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II launch is visible 30-40 seconds after liftoff across central Florida, including Orlando, Treasure Coast, and potentially up to Gainesville and Sarasota.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: '3: Launch + 30 seconds, ... Orlando, ... Treasure Coast, ... Central Florida ...; 4: Launch + 40 seconds, ... Gainesville, Sarasota'
verifications.reasoning: Precise time-area matches in visibility map.

verifications.claim: Visibility of the Artemis II launch extends 50+ seconds after liftoff to Jacksonville, West Palm Beach, and into southern Georgia (Valdosta/Brunswick).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: '5: Launch + 50 seconds, ... Jacksonville, ... West Palm Beach, ... Brunswick, Georgia, and Valdosta, Georgia'
verifications.reasoning: Exact cities and 50+ seconds directly listed.

verifications.claim: FOX 35 Orlando provides a detailed map showing specific city views.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: from 'fox35orlando.com'; 'NASA released an image showing how visible ... In the graphic above'; title includes 'visibility map: These Florida, Georgia cities'
verifications.reasoning: R4 is the FOX 35 Orlando article providing the map with cities.

verifications.claim: Best in-person viewing of the Artemis II launch is east of I-95 in the Space Coast region (e.g., Titusville, Cocoa Beach).
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: Sources mention best viewing on Space Coast (including Titusville, Cocoa Beach), but no mention of 'east of I-95'.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II launch can be streamed live on NASA's YouTube.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'NASA+ ... from its official site and YouTube'; R3: 'on its YouTube page'
verifications.reasoning: Direct statements of live streaming on NASA's YouTube.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II launch can be streamed live on X (formerly Twitter).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.reasoning: Explicit mention of livestream on X.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II rocket may be visible for up to 3.5 minutes.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R2/R4/R5: visibility up to 70 seconds or 40,000 feet; R4: 'three-and-a-half minutes after launch to be heard' (sound, not visibility)
verifications.reasoning: Sources cap visibility at 70 seconds; 3.5 minutes (210s) contradicts and confuses with sound range.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II rocket will be visible until it hits roughly 40,000 feet in altitude.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'Once the rocket reaches 40,000 feet, it will be out of the visibility range, NASA said.'
